You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

1. Your action is read only from the plain text of your reply, never from Python output or a tool call: printing JSON in Python or calling a tool named submit/request_demos/finish/answer does nothing. Keep each turn to a few tool calls, then reply in text ending with exactly one of {"action": "request_demos"}, {"action": "submit", "grid": [[ints]]}, {"action": "finish"} on the last line. Replies without a valid action waste the turn, and a few in a row end the puzzle charged in full.
2. When a message says "Decide now" or "could not find a valid action", make no tool call: reply at once in text with the action line. Submit only a grid already printed above (copy it); otherwise send {"action": "request_demos"}. You have not submitted anything until you see a verdict message.
3. With no demo pair yet, request_demos first: the test input alone cannot show the rule, so never submit before seeing a demo.
4. Never retype grids. Load every grid shown so far (rerun after each new demo):
```
import os,glob,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])   # this instance's own log: the folder keeps every earlier one's
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
```
5. Write the rule as a Python function f and check f(demo input) == demo output for every demo pair. Submit only when all match, pasting the printed json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])). If one mismatches, fix f or request another demo; never resubmit a grid already judged wrong.
6. Once f matches every demo, submit instead of requesting more demos.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a library in the folder /home/USER/runs/paper/qwen-hpl-u1-turns/frozen/seen-3/play/users/u020/system/state/workspace/programs, two files per task, named for its task id: /home/USER/runs/paper/qwen-hpl-u1-turns/frozen/seen-3/play/users/u020/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py, defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid; and /home/USER/runs/paper/qwen-hpl-u1-turns/frozen/seen-3/play/users/u020/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.json, every demonstration pair received for the task, as a list of {"input": grid, "output": grid}. # Define the transform based on my analysis
def transform(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    # Start with a copy of the input
    output = [[grid[r][c] for c in range(cols)] for r in range(rows)]
    
    # Find all non-bg cells
    non_bg = set()
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if grid[r][c] != bg:
                non_bg.add((r, c))
    
    # Find all diagonal pairs with the same value
    # A pair (r1,c1), (r2,c2) is on a diagonal if |r1-r2| == |c1-c2|
    for i in range(len(non_bg)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(non_bg)):
            r1, c1 = non_bg[i]
            r2, c2 = non_bg[j]
            
            if abs(r1-r2) == abs(c1-c2) and (r1,r2) not in [(2,1),(1,2), (1,1),(2,2)]:
                # Both cells have the same value (they do by definition)
                # Check direction and fill backwards
                dr, dc = r2 - r1, c2 - c1
                
                # Check if this is a valid diagonal (not too close)
                if abs(dr) > 1 or abs(dc) > 1:
                    continue
                    
                # Find the "first" cell of this diagonal (min rank in the direction of fill)
                # We fill backwards, so we start from the cell with smaller r if dr>0
                # or larger r if dr < 0
                if dr == 0 and dc != 0:
                    # Horizontal - not diagonal
                    continue
                elif dr != 0 and dc == 0:
                    # Vertical - not diagonal
                    continue
                    
                # Get the direction to fill backwards (opposite to the direction between cells)
                if dr > 0:
                    fill_dr, fill_dc = -dr, -dc
                elif dr < 0:
                    fill_dr, fill_dc = -dr, -dc
                # Horizontal strides are handled separately
                
                # Fill backwards from the first cell
                curr_r, curr_c = r1, c1
                for _ in range(abs(dr)):  # Fill abs(dr) times
                    new_r, new_c = curr_r + fill_dr, curr_c + fill_dc
                    if 0 <= new_r < rows and 0 <= new_c < cols:
                        output[new_r][new_c] = grid[r1][c1]
                    curr_r += fill_dr
                    curr_c += fill_dc
    
    return output

]

# Anti-diagonal (c+r) might be the key
bg = 1
rows, cols = 7, 15

def transform(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    output = [[grid[r][c] for c in range(cols)] for r in range(rows)]
    
    # Group by anti-diagonal (c+r) and value
    anti_diags = {}
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                key = (c + r, v)
                if key not in anti_diags:
                    anti_diags[key] = []
                anti_diags[key].append((r, c))
    
    print("Anti-diagonal groups:")
    for (anti_diag, val), positions in anti_diags.items():
        print(f"  c+r={anti_diag}, value={val}: {positions} (len={len(positions)})")
        if len(positions) >= 2:
            print(f"    → Would fill with {val}")
            for r in range(rows):
                c = anti_diag - r
                if 0 <= c < cols and grid[r][c] == bg:
                    output[r][c] = val
    
    return output

result = transform(test_input)

print("\nResult:")
for i, row in enumerate(result):

def transform(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    output = [[bg] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    
    # Copy all non-background cells
    non_bg = set()
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:

        if v == bg:
            continue
        positions = [(r, c) for r in range(rows) for c in range(cols) if grid[r][c] == v]
        if len(positions) < 2:

        # Group by main diagonal (c-r)
        by_md = defaultdict(list)
        for r, c in positions:
            by_md[c - r].append((r, c))
        
        # Find diagonals with 2+ cells
        for md, cells in by_md.items():
            if len(cells) >= 2:
                # Fill entire main diagonal UP-LEFT from min position
                min_pos = min(cells)  # min by (r, c)
                max_pos = max(cells)  # max by (r, c)
                
                # Fill FROM max_pos UP-LEFT to min_pos and beyond

import json

def transform(grid):
    """
    ARC-style transformation rule:
    - For each non-background value that appears in 2+ cells, find the line through them
    - Extend that line to fill the full diagonal across the grid
    - Background = grid[0][0]
    """
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    # Collect all positions by value
    positions_by_value = {}
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                if v not in positions_by_value:
                    positions_by_value[v] = []
                positions_by_value[v].append((r, c))
    
    # Result grid - start with background
    result = [[bg] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    
    # Copy all original non-background cells
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                result[r][c] = v
    
    # For each value, if multiple positions, find and extend the line
    for v, positions in positions_by_value.items():
        if len(positions) < 2:
            continue  # Single position stays as-is
        
        # Find the line through these positions
        # For ARC, positions form either horizontal, vertical, or diagonal lines
        r1, c1 = positions[0]
        r2, c2 = positions[1]
        dr, dc = r2 - r1, c2 - c1
        
        if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
            continue  # Same position
        
        # Reduce to unit vector
        gcd_tables = [(1,1), (1,-1), (-1,1), (-1,-1)]
        extent = max(max(abs(r2-r1)), max(abs(c2-c1)))
        factor = extent
        dr //= factor
        dc //= factor
        
        # Find endpoints of the line
        r_min, r_max = min(positions, key=lambda p: p[0])[0], max(positions, key=lambda p: p[0])[0]
        c_min, c_max = min(positions, key=lambda p: p[1])[1], max(positions, key=lambda p: p[1])[1]
        
        # Start from endpoint going against the direction
        if dr > 0:
            extend_r, extend_c = r_min - 1, c_min - 1 if dc < 0 else c_min + 1
        elif dr < 0:
            extend_r, extend_c = r_max + 1, c_max + 1 if dc > 0 else c_max - 1
        else:
            extend_r, extend_c = r_min - 1, c_min - 1
        
        # Fill in the full line
        curr_r, curr_c = extend_r, extend_c
        while 0 <= curr_r < rows and 0 <= curr_c < cols:
            result[curr_r][curr_c] = v
            curr_r += dr
            curr_c += dc
    
    return result

# Key insight: the positions are collected in row-major order
# So for [6,14] and [7,13], the order is [(6,14), (7,13)]
# dr = 1, dc = -1

# For a DOWN diagonal (dr>0), we extend from position[0] going backwards
# and from position[1] going forwards
# But we should only extend through BACKGROUND cells
# And we stop when we hit a NON-background cell

import json

def transform(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    positions_by_value = {}
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                if v not in positions_by_value:
                    positions_by_value[v] = []
                positions_by_value[v].append((r, c))
    
    result = [[bg] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    
    # First, copy all original non-background cells
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                result[r][c] = v
    
    # Now extend diagonals
    for v, positions in positions_by_value.items():
        if len(positions) < 2:
            continue  # Single cell - no extension
        
        positions = sorted(positions)  # Sort by (row, col)
        pos1, pos2 = positions[0], positions[1]
        r1, c1 = pos1
        r2, c2 = pos2
        
        dr, dc = r2 - r1, c2 - c1
        
        # Only extend if on diagonal
        if abs(dr) != abs(dc) or dr == 0:
            continue
        
        step_r = dr // abs(dr)
        step_c = dc // abs(dc)
        
        # UP-LEFT (against the flow) from pos1
        r, c = r1, c1
        while True:
            new_r = r - step_r
            new_c = c - step_c
            if not (0 <= new_r < rows and 0 <= new_c < cols):
                break
            if result[new_r][new_c] != bg:
                break  # Hit non-background, stop
            result[new_r][new_c] = v
            r, c = new_r, new_c
        
        # DOWN-RIGHT (with the flow) from pos2
        r, c = r2, c2
        while True:
            new_r = r + step_r
            new_c = c + step_c
            if not (0 <= new_r < rows and 0 <= new_c < cols):
                break
            if result[new_r][new_c] != bg:
                break  # Hit non-background, stop
            result[new_r][new_c] = v
            r, c = new_r, new_c
    
    return result

def transform_fixed(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    # Find positions by value
    from collections import defaultdict
    positions = defaultdict(list)
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                positions[v].append((r, c))
    
    # Create result grid with background
    result = [[bg] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    
    # Copy original non-background cells
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                result[r][c] = v
    
    # Extend diagonals
    for v, pos_list in positions.items():
        if len(pos_list) < 2:
            continue
        
        pos_list = sorted(pos_list)  # Sort by position
        # But we need to assign pos1, pos2 based on WHICH STARTS THE LINE
        # If dr, dc > 0: pos1 is the "top-left" one, pos2 is "bottom-right"
        # If dr, dc < 0: opposite
        # Let me recalculate: for 5 at (4,13),(5,14), dr=1,dc=1
        # So going from (4,13) to (5,14): apply (1,1)
        # That means pos1 is the one BEFORE the step, pos2 is AFTER the step
        
        r_min, c_min = pos_list[0]  # (4,13)
        r_max, c_max = pos_list[1]  # (5,14)
        
        # Check if pos_max = pos_min + (dr, dc)
        # (5,14) - (4,13) = (1,1) ✓
        dr, dc = r_max - r_min, c_max - c_min
        
        # For the line, step is (dr, dc) if |dr|==|dc|
        step_r = 1 if dr > 0 else (-1 if dr < 0 else 0)
        step_c = 1 if dc > 0 else (-1 if dc < 0 else 0)
        
        if step_r == 0 or step_c == 0 or abs(dr) != abs(dc):
            continue
        
        # Now check extend directions:
        # From pos_max, continue in (+step_r, +step_c) direction
        # From pos_min, continue in (-step_r, -step_c) direction
        
        # Check backward from pos_min (going against step)
        r, c = r_min, c_min
        while True:
            nr, nc = r - step_r, c - step_c
            if not (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols):
                break
            if result[nr][nc] != bg:
                break
            result[nr][nc] = v
            r, c = nr, nc
        
        # Check forward from pos_max (continuing step)
        r, c = r_max, c_max
        while True:
            nr, nc = r + step_r, c + step_c
            if not (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols):
                break
            if result[nr][nc] != bg:
                break
            result[nr][nc] = v
            r, c = nr, nc
    
    return result

def transform_final(grid):
    """
    ARC transformation rule for task-35d6465a:
    - For each value with 2+ diagonal positions (dr=±dc≠0):
      - Check if backward from pos1 can fill (all bg)
      - Check if forward from pos2 can fill (all bg)
      - Only fill if BOTH directions can fill (not blocked)
    - Boundary is OK (just means 0 cells filled), non-bg blocks fill
    """
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = grid[0][0]
    
    from collections import defaultdict
    positions = defaultdict(list)
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                positions[v].append((r, c))
    
    result = [[bg] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    
    # Copy original non-background cells
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v != bg:
                result[r][c] = v
    
    # Extend diagonals
    for v, pos_list in positions.items():
        if len(pos_list) < 2:
            continue
        
        pos_list = sorted(pos_list)
        pos1, pos2 = pos_list[0], pos_list[1]
        r1, c1 = pos1
        r2, c2 = pos2
        
        dr, dc = r2 - r1, c2 - c1
        if dr == 0 or dc == 0 or abs(dr) != abs(dc):
            continue
        
        step_r = 1 if dr > 0 else -1
        step_c = 1 if dc > 0 else -1
        
        # Check backward from pos1
        backward_blocked = False
        r, c = r1, c1
        while True:
            nr, nc = r - step_r, c - step_c
            if not (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols):
                backward_blocked = False  # boundary is OK
                break
            if result[nr][nc] != bg:
                backward_blocked = True  # non-bg blocks
                break
            r, c = nr, nc
        
        # Check forward from pos2
        forward_blocked = False
        r, c = r2, c2
        while True:
            nr, nc = r + step_r, c + step_c
            if not 0 <= nr < rows or not 0 <= nc < cols:
                forward_blocked = False  # boundary is OK
                break
            if result[nr][nc] != bg:
                forward_blocked = True  # non-bg blocks
                break
            r, c = nr, nc
        
        # Only fill if BOTH directions can fill
        if not backward_blocked and not forward_blocked:
            # Fill backward
            r, c = r1, c1
            while True:
                nr, nc = r - step_r, c - step_c
                if not (0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols):
                    break
                if result[nr][nc] != bg:
                    break
                result[nr][nc] = v
                r, c = nr, nc
            
            # Fill forward
            r, c = r2, c2
            while True:
                nr, nc = r + step_r, c + step_c
                if not 0 <= nr < rows or not 0 <= nc < cols:
                    break
                if result[nr][nc] != bg:
                    break
                result[nr][nc] = v
                r, c = nr, nc
    
    return result
